execution: 64 fresh actual HTTP documents in the collaborative browser with physical ImageData uploads and native ArrayBuffer.transfer
limitations: putImageData uses Nimbo's own Rust bitmap backend and physical typed-array input; no browser renderer or GPU backend is invoked.

extremeDirty differs in every variant: Nimbo normalizes [-2147483648 width starting at 2147483647] in checked i64 arithmetic and writes the intersecting source; Chromium does not return the expected pixels. This discrepancy remains unresolved.

opaque differs in every variant: Nimbo preserves alpha:false storage as premultiplied RGB with alpha 255. Chromium's willReadFrequently:true context returns [255,0,0,128,0,0,0,0] after uploading red alpha 128 and white alpha 0. The default context separately returns [255,0,0,128,255,255,255,0]. No universal opaque-upload parity is claimed.

Detached storage is tested through actual ArrayBuffer.transfer, including a zero-area dirty rectangle and numeric-conversion precedence. SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable in this browser document and is not covered by this comparison.

The scope covers sRGB RGBA8 uploads, dirty/source/destination clipping, replacement, live input data, snapshots, argument/brand checks, byte offsets, captured intrinsic copies and resource rejection/recovery. Full Canvas 2D, transforms, clipping paths, images, text, encoding, screenshots and WebGL remain missing.
